w:r.w:t: Skip the Queue. Not the Food.

WUKWAY is a local food pre-ordering and pickup platform focused on India's offline food economy — street thelas, small restaurants, stalls, and quick-service shops. Unlike Swiggy or Zomato, WUKWAY does not deliver food. Customers discover nearby outlets on foot, order and pay in advance, declare how far away they are, and walk in to collect a ready order using a pickup token — skipping the physical waiting queue entirely.
no riders, no delivery logistics, no delivery SLAs. This removes the single biggest cost and operational complexity of a food-delivery business.
outlets are surfaced by walking time, not driving distance — built for dense Indian markets, college areas, office lanes and street-food clusters.
the core value proposition is “order ahead, skip the line,” which is a fundamentally different problem from “get food delivered.”
small vendors keep the full ticket price minus a lightweight commission/subscription — no delivery commission stacked on top.

This is a build specification for the engineering team. It defines every app, every feature, the data model, the recommended technology stack, hosting architecture on AWS, and a phased MVP roadmap. Section 12 lists open product decisions the team should confirm with you before or during Phase 1.
WUKWAY is a two-sided marketplace with an operations layer, which means three distinct applications share one backend:
Discover outlets, order ahead, track pickup
Receive orders, manage menu, mark order status
Onboard outlets, manage cities, offers, commissions, support

8.5 Why Not Serverless-First (Lambda) for the API

Lambda + API Gateway is viable and can be cheaper at very low volume, but the WebSocket-driven, session-heavy nature of live order tracking is simpler to reason about and debug on always-on containers (ECS Fargate) in the early stage. Revisit serverless once traffic patterns are well understood — it's a valid Phase 2+ cost optimization, not a Phase 1 requirement.

10. Open Questions for the Team / You to Decide
Flagging these now avoids rework later — worth a short decision call before Phase 1 kicks off.
Payment timing: does the customer pay in full at order confirmation, or only pay at pickup (cash/UPI on collection)? This materially changes the refund and no-show handling logic.
No-show handling: what happens if a customer declares ETA, the vendor prepares food, and the customer never arrives? Needs a policy (e.g. hold slot for X minutes, partial charge).
Vendor onboarding model: will WUKWAY ops onboard vendors manually (door-to-door, likely for MVP) or self-serve via the Admin/Vendor app?
Commission vs. subscription: flat monthly fee per outlet, or a % commission per order — or a hybrid?
Vendor App form factor: is a low-cost Android tablet provided to vendors, or should it also work as a simple web page on any phone/laptop they already have?

Build order: Customer App core loop → Vendor App core loop → Admin approval tooling → payments → real-time status → everything else in Phase 2/3. The Order state machine in Figure 4.3 is the contract between all three apps — get that right first and the rest of the build follows naturally.
